documents.title: Using AI Technology Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-level guidance from the Faculty Development Center setting principles for AI use: verification, academic integrity, privacy, and instructor clarity. It makes no ban or permission itself and leaves rules to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The page sets principles ("all users must review and verify", "Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use") but no rule on whether AI is allowed, so it leaves the decision to instructors: delegates.

units.why: The rationale sentence states the campus commitment and scope: "CSUF is committed to supporting teaching, learning, research, and service." It is an institution-level purpose statement, so P56, informs, general.
units.anchor: CSUF is committed to supporting teaching, learning, research, and service.

units.why: "requires a reflective approach, including consideration of biases and inaccuracies" names bias and ethical concerns about GAI, so P53 (informs); P31 does not fit since it is not directed at verifying output here.
units.anchor: The use of GAI tools requires a reflective approach, including consideration of biases and inaccuracies
units.policy: The use of GAI tools requires a reflective approach, including consideration of biases and inaccuracies in AI output, as well as ethical use of these technologies.

units.why: "should be transparent about its use" asks the whole University community to be open about AI use; this is a disclosure expectation, P24, with a soft "should".
units.anchor: should be transparent about its use
units.policy: The University community should be transparent about its use of generative AI.

units.why: "Provide ongoing support for the responsible use of Generative AI by faculty, staff, and students" is a campus-level commitment to support, which sets framework principles (P56); P63 is specific to faculty workshops and does not cover students.
units.anchor: Provide ongoing support for the responsible use of Generative AI by faculty, staff, and students.

units.why: "all users must review and verify AI generated content" directly requires verification because AI output is inaccurate, so P31, must, applying to all users.
units.anchor: all users must review and verify AI generated content
units.policy: All users must review and verify AI generated content before using it for teaching, learning, scholarly and creative activity, or other purposes.

units.why: "Generative AI detectors, which have been proven to be unreliable and biased" says detectors are unreliable, so P39, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI detectors, which have been proven to be unreliable and biased

units.why: "conforming to CSUF policy when using AI technologies" ties AI use to existing academic honesty rules as a campus principle; P56 (principles) fits better than P36, which needs misconduct classification or process.
units.anchor: Uphold academic honesty and integrity by conforming to CSUF policy when using AI technologies
units.policy: Users uphold academic honesty and integrity by conforming to CSUF policy when using AI technologies, ensuring AI assistance enhances learning and scholarly and creative activity without compromising the authenticity of academic work or assessments.

units.why: "Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use" asks instructors to state expectations to students, so P09, should, course-start.
units.anchor: Instructors should provide clear guidance for acceptable AI use.

units.why: "Maintain transparency in the integration of AI tools for teaching" asks people integrating AI into teaching to be open about it, an instructor disclosure expectation, P47 (should).
units.anchor: Maintain transparency in the integration of AI tools for teaching, scholarly and creative activity, and

units.why: "safeguarding confidential information and user intellectual property" is a privacy and data-security directive, P50, should, for all users.
units.anchor: Prioritize safeguarding confidential information and user intellectual property
units.policy: Prioritize safeguarding confidential information and user intellectual property by following established policies on data security and privacy to prevent unauthorized access or misuse of sensitive data.

units.why: "educate users to recognize and guard against AI-driven phishing attempts or scams" asks for user education about AI security threats, closest to P50 data protection.
units.anchor: educate users to recognize and guard against AI-driven phishing attempts or scams

documents.title: Creating a Generative AI Policy
tiers: Use of Generative AI by Assignment (model)
documents.summary: Instructor guidance for writing syllabus AI policies, with three sample policy models and a five-level AI continuum, plus advice on redesigning assessments. Faculty decide the level.
documents.stance_why: "Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools" and the page offers templates and a five-level continuum, so it sets tiers and delegates.

units.why: "Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools in their classes and even individual assignments" puts the decision with instructors and assignments, so P04.
units.anchor: Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of these tools
units.policy: Each faculty member is empowered to determine the appropriate use of AI tools in their classes and even individual assignments.

units.why: "Including transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions ... is essential" tells instructors to put the AI rule in the syllabus and assignments, P09.
units.anchor: Including transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions specifying under what circumstances the use
units.policy: Instructors include transparent language in the syllabus and assignment instructions specifying under what circumstances the use of AI/Tech tools is permitted.

units.why: "Students must adhere to the syllabus" binds students to the instructor-set rules; it follows the per-instructor model (P04), not P29 which is about owning submitted work.
units.anchor: Students must adhere to the syllabus to ensure their usage of AI/Tech tools
units.frag_start: Students must adhere to the syllabus

units.why: The list item "Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden" is a consideration instructors should address in the policy, P09.
units.anchor: Under what circumstances AI use is permitted or forbidden

units.why: "How students should cite or credit AI" is a listed item for the policy; it concerns citation of AI, so P24 (instructor should cover it).
units.anchor: How students should cite or credit AI

units.why: "consider providing a warning about the technology's tendency toward hallucination" asks instructors to warn about false output, P31, should.
units.anchor: A notice about using AI ethically and responsibly
units.frag_start: A notice about using AI ethically

units.why: "the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to produce content" says AI should support learning and not replace it, P32.
units.anchor: Discussion of the need to use AI as a tool to learn, not just to
units.frag_start: Discussion of the need to use

units.frag_start: As a best practice, faculty are encouraged

units.why: The no-AI model says "students must be the author of all work. The use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, is not permitted," a default ban for the course, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, is not permitted.
units.policy: For this course, students must be the author of all work. The use of generative AI, such as ChatGPT, is not permitted.

units.why: "Use of these tools will be considered a violation of the CSUF Academic Dishonesty Policies" classifies unauthorized AI as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Use of these tools will be considered a violation of the
units.policy: Use of these tools will be considered a violation of the CSUF Academic Dishonesty Policies and may be subject to disciplinary action.

units.why: "many tools students use daily incorporate AI features, which can sometimes be overlooked" is about AI built into everyday software (Grammarly, Word), so P07, informs.
units.anchor: many tools students use daily incorporate AI features, which can sometimes be overlooked
units.frag_start: As educators, it's essential to be aware

units.why: "consider specifying whether the use of such AI tools is allowed or prohibited" asks instructors to rule on AI features within common tools, P07.
units.anchor: consider specifying whether the use of such AI tools is allowed or prohibited

units.frag_start: Please do not use AI tools
units.policy: Students may not use AI tools like ChatGPT for generating text or Microsoft Copilot for drafting content on this assignment.

units.why: The minor-use model says "You may use AI in some minor ways" such as "generate ideas ... create an outline", a brainstorming permission, P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI in some minor ways.

units.why: The same model lists "polish or edit text you have drafted" as acceptable, a prose-support permission, P18.
units.anchor: polish or edit text you have drafted
units.policy: Students may use AI to polish or edit text they have drafted, where the faculty lists it as acceptable.

units.why: "quiz yourself, or for other studying purposes" permits AI for study aids and self-checking, P14.

units.policy: Students may not use AI to generate content that is directly used in an assignment (such as code, text, images, or other media) or to solve problems from assignments.

units.why: "for any purpose while taking a quiz or test" bans AI during assessments, P22.
units.anchor: for any purpose while taking a quiz or test
units.policy: Students may not use AI for any purpose while taking a quiz or test.

units.why: "Always review individual assignments for specific instructions" tells students rules vary by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Always review individual assignments for specific instructions.

units.why: The optional statement says language from an AI app must be put "in quotation marks and adding a citation", a disclosure requirement, P24.
units.anchor: you must properly attribute that use by putting that language in quotation marks and adding

units.policy: If you use language generated by an AI app, you must properly attribute that use by putting that language in quotation marks and adding a citation.

units.policy: Where the faculty requires it, students keep drafts of assignments and generative AI logs that demonstrate how they used AI and what portion of the assignment content was generated by AI.

units.why: This framing paragraph repeats the campus purpose: "The University community should investigate where and when generative AI might be appropriate," an institution-level principle, P56.

documents.title: CSUF's AI Policy
documents.summary: Student-facing library statement that CSUF has no campus-wide AI policy and that each instructor decides. It points to campus guidelines.
documents.stance_why: "Whether AI is allowed or prohibited in your class is up to your individual Instructor" hands the decision to instructors: delegates.

units.why: "There is no campus-wide policy on AI at CSUF!" states there is no single institutional rule, which is the instructor-decides model, P04.
units.anchor: There is no campus-wide policy on AI at CSUF!

units.why: "Whether AI is allowed or prohibited in your class is up to your individual Instructor" assigns the decision to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Whether AI is allowed or prohibited in your class is up to your individual Instructor.
units.frag_start: Whether AI is allowed or prohibited

units.why: "always follow whatever your Instructor states is the class policy on AI" tells students to obey the class rule, stated verbally or in writing, P04.

notes: No college or computing-unit AI policy found; course layer deferred. All three documents are university-layer and delegate to instructors. Template placeholders ([faculty insert ...]) in the sample policy models were coded as the model's content, with modality reflecting that faculty choose to include them.
